chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ḥanān ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Ṭarīf ibn Sinān al-Thawrī, who said:
I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام about a man who stole a free woman and sold her. He said:

“In it there are four prescribed punishments. As for the first of them: he is a thief, so his hand is cut off. The second: if he had intercourse with her, he is flogged. And regarding the one who bought her, if he had intercourse with her while knowing, then if he is muḥṣan, he is stoned, and if he is not muḥṣan, he is given the prescribed flogging. But if he did not know, then there is nothing upon him. As for her, if he forced her, then there is nothing upon her; but if she complied, she is given the prescribed flogging.”

key_terms.تُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ: his hand is cut off as the punishment for theft
key_terms.حُرَّةً: a free woman, not a slave
key_terms.رُجِمَ: he is stoned as the hadd punishment
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through prior or current valid marriage, affecting the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on one who steals and sells a free woman, and on those involved if intercourse occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the theft and sale of a free woman and the resulting penal consequences for the thief, the buyer, and the woman depending on knowledge, coercion, and marital status. It highlights the application of hudud in cases involving theft, unlawful intercourse, and coercion, distinguishing between deliberate wrongdoing and absence of culpability.
